cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.3.5
cuerpo.body:
**Zangetsu 2.3.5**

A small update focused on offline access, startup, and TV fixes.

- **Offline profile unlock:** Use a profile’s saved PIN offline after unlocking that profile online once on the same device.
- **Faster offline startup:** Reduced startup waits when the internet is unavailable or your connection is unresponsive.
- **Choose how the app opens:** Turn off “Ask on launch” to open your active profile directly. Switching to a locked profile still asks for its PIN.
- **TV Source Health fix:** Use your remote to move through source results and scroll the page.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.3.4
cuerpo.body:
**Zangetsu 2.3.4**

A refreshed look, easier downloads, voice search, and more ways to enjoy your favourite content.

- **Mangayomi extension support:** Add repositories and use supported anime, manga, and novel sources. Includes language filters, adult-source filtering, extension updates, and Popular/Latest browsing.
- **New liquid-glass navigation:** Customize the glass tint, blur, and background visibility. The new visibility slider is optional and starts off.
- **Faster shortcuts:** Long-press Profile to switch profiles, double-tap it to open Settings, and optionally add Search to your navbar.
- **Voice search on Android and iOS:** Search by speaking, with an animated listening screen, live text feedback, and clearer retry messages.
- **Profile protection:** Set a 4- or 6-digit PIN that works across devices, with optional fingerprint or Face ID unlock on supported devices.
- **Redesigned Downloads:** A cleaner library-style layout with posters, episode thumbnails, search, and swipeable tabs.
- **Better offline watching:** Downloaded episodes play as a season queue, with improved episode ordering and TV playback.
- **Easier download management:** Select multiple episodes—or select all—to delete. Download options now show estimated size and available storage.
- **Discord Rich Presence improvements:** Improved connection and activity updates, a simpler settings screen, a better preview, and a fix for the crash when switching it off.
- **Softer adaptive colours:** More balanced artwork-based backgrounds on Home and detail screens, alongside smoother detail-screen opening.
- **More viewing options:** Optional title logos on supported detail pages, a preferred starting orientation for the Android native player, and improved touch controls.
- **Remembered source choices:** Home now remembers your selected source catalogue separately for each content mode.
- **Reading improvements:** A less intrusive manga page counter and an option to keep episode lists reversed.
- **New appearance defaults:** Edge banner, Bankai splash, System font, and liquid navigation. Your saved choices stay unchanged.
- **Other fixes:** Improved offline profile loading, more reliable GIF avatar search, fewer repeated notification prompts, and fixes for clipped poster titles.

*PIN-locked profiles require an internet connection to unlock.*

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.3.3
cuerpo.body:
### Home & browsing
- Browse source catalogues directly from Home and search within the selected catalogue.
- Smoother catalogue and detail-screen transitions, with improved AniList poster images.
- Cleaner Sources screen and easier access to provider settings.

### Profiles
- Manage profiles with custom photo or GIF avatars, bios, and individual app colors.
- Sign in to save items to My List or upload profile images. Continue Watching and Reading remain available while signed out.

### Playback & downloads
- Auto Resolve shows which source it is checking, can be stopped, and checks up to 20 sources.
- Clearer loading and retry options in the phone player.
- Downloaded episodes show progress, subtitles, and quality.
- Improved Continue Watching on TV and clearer TV navigation.

### Cloud Sync
- Cloud sync now runs through a new Zangetsu server, syncing lists, profiles, and watch/reading progress across devices.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.2.0
cuerpo.body:
A new look, streaming services you can browse, and a manga reader that stops eating your phone's memory.

### A new look

- **New icon and splash.** The crescent mark replaces the old icon everywhere: your launcher, the install screen, notifications, and the Android TV banner
- **You can pick your splash** in Settings → Appearance. Wordmark by default, or an animated one if you want it

### Streaming services

- **Browse by service.** See what Netflix, Prime, Disney+ and the rest carry in your country, from Search or straight off the home screen
- **Your country is picked automatically.** There's an override in Settings if it guesses wrong
- **On Android TV too**, as a row on the home screen, with the full list behind See All
- Titles still play through your own sources. This is for finding something to watch, not for streaming from those services

### The manga reader

- **Tall pages don't eat your memory any more.** A long manhwa page used to be decoded whole, however big it was. Now only the part on screen gets decoded, at the zoom you're at
- **Keep reading into the next chapter** without dropping back to the chapter list
- **Long-press a chapter to mark it read.** You can also open a chapter on the source's own site
- **Export downloaded chapters as EPUB.** Downloaded novel chapters keep their images now, so they read properly offline

### Finding a source

- **Source Priority, rebuilt.** One numbered list, a line showing where the app stops looking, and a slider for how many sources to try
- **Every source says why it's there** — "played 47 times", "hasn't worked recently" — so you're not guessing which ones are any good
- **Sources are asked in parallel.** One that just answers slowly is no longer written off as empty
- **A show is looked up under both its names**, so sources that only list the English title aren't missed
- **Dead sources get noticed.** A source that searches fine but has stopped producing a video is flagged on Source health, with a button to uninstall it
- **Source icons show up everywhere**: the picker, the installed list, every sources screen

### Trackers

- **MangaBaka added** as a fourth tracker, for reading

### Fixed

- **Your list could be thrown away.** One corrupt storage box was deleted outright, and My List went with it. Now it's kept and repaired
- **Audio kept playing for five to ten seconds** after you closed a video
- **The home screen loaded twice and cached its own failure**, so a blip on your connection left it empty until you restarted
- **The reconnect banner never went away** once a momentary drop raised it
- **A finished episode or chapter only dimmed after a restart**
- **Open in browser gave you a 404** on sources that had changed their URL scheme. The app was guessing the address; now it asks the source
- **A source you picked by hand isn't swapped out** when one of its links dies
- **The globe in Z Mode never worked**
- **An extension that failed to install said nothing about why**
- **The source language filter did nothing**

### Android TV

- **The streaming services row** reaches the full list through See All
- **Source settings work with a remote**
- **Season chips and Auto Resolve progress** match the phone

### iOS

- **4K stuttered because the app asked for a decoder iOS doesn't have.** It was asking for Android's. Now it asks for VideoToolbox, so 4K is hardware-decoded

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.1.3 (beta)
cuerpo.body:
Finding a source is faster, finds more, and you can now tell the app how hard to look.

This is a **beta**. The Source Priority screen is new, and the TV version of it has not been tried on a TV yet — that is the part worth telling us about.

### Faster

- **When nothing has a show, you find out in seconds.** Before, the app quietly worked through every source you had installed, one at a time. Now it tries your best few and stops
- **You choose how many.** A slider from 3 to 10 in Source Priority. Fewer means you stop waiting sooner; more means a better chance of finding something rare
- **It asks a few sources at the same time** instead of waiting for each one in turn

### Finds more

- **Slow sources are no longer skipped.** Some sources take a few seconds to answer. The app used to give up on them and tell you nothing was there — even though picking that same source by hand played the episode fine. It waits properly now
- **Shows are looked up by both names.** Plenty of sources list an anime by its English name, so asking only for the Japanese one came back empty. Both are tried now

### Source Priority, rebuilt

- **One list you can actually read.** Numbered, with a line showing where the app stops looking
- **Every source tells you why it is there** — "played 47 times", or "hasn't worked recently" — so you are not guessing which ones are any good
- **Drag your favourite to the top** and it stays. Everything else keeps sorting itself, so you do not have to arrange the whole list
- **The old on/off switches are gone.** Dragging a source below the line does the same job. If you had switched sources off before, they are back on

### Home

- **The banner fills in straight away.** The genres and episode count used to sit blank while the app looked for a source — sometimes for quite a while — even though none of that comes from a source

### Android TV

- **Same screen, built for a remote.** Arrows instead of dragging, plus and minus instead of the slider
- **It no longer claims no source has a show** when only your top few were checked

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.1.2 (beta)
cuerpo.body:
Tall manhwa pages stopped eating memory, downloaded novels finally keep their pictures, and you can take a novel out as an EPUB.

This is a **beta**. The reader was rebuilt underneath — it has been read with, but the phones it helps most are the ones we could not test on. Reports welcome.

### Manga reading

- **A tall page no longer loads all of itself to show you one screen.** A long manhwa page was decoded whole — around 25MB of it — just to draw the part in front of you. Only the visible piece is decoded now, at the resolution your screen actually shows, so the same page costs roughly a third of what it did. The picture is identical; there is simply less of it held at once. Short manga pages are untouched, because there was nothing there to save
- **Reading carries on into the next chapter** instead of stopping at the end of one
- **Pages load one at a time, nearest first**, so the page you are looking at is not queued behind five you have not reached
- **Chapter page lists are remembered**, so going back to a chapter does not re-fetch it
- **Edges are trimmed more accurately**, using the page's real content box

### Novels

- **Export a novel as EPUB.** A new button on the novel page turns your downloaded chapters into a proper `.epub` — pick the file name, the folder, all chapters or a range, and whether titles carry their chapter number. Only downloaded chapters can be included, since they are the only ones held on the device
- **Downloaded chapters keep their pictures.** Images inside a chapter were left pointing at the web, so offline they were broken. They are saved alongside the text now, and removed with the chapter when you delete it

### Fixed

- **A source you pinned by hand is no longer swapped out** when one of its links dies
- **Simkl showed no tracking state for films and series**, and reloaded your whole library more often than it needed to
- **The default cut is no longer pinned** when a title has no sub/dub toggle to pin it with
- **Leaving a screen stops its loading** rather than leaving it queued behind you

### Android TV

- **The browse-sources screen follows the D-pad properly** — focus, the search field and the tabs behave like the rest of the 10-foot screens (thanks to Nathen Brewer)

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.1.1
cuerpo.body:
A week's worth of "it froze", "it won't play", and "that button does nothing" — traced to their actual causes.

### Fixed

- **The Cloudflare button could never work.** Any 403 from a Cloudflare-fronted host was treated as a challenge, including ordinary blocks with nothing to solve. The source was then skipped entirely, and the button opened a page with no challenge in it. Now it has to actually be a challenge — and when you solve one, the source is genuinely let back in
- **Backing out of a video hung for up to 25 seconds.** Leaving only stopped the *next* source; the one already being tried ran to its full time limit first. It's under three seconds now, and leaving no longer benches your pinned source for ten minutes
- **A source that still works no longer gets given up on.** A source you picked yourself gets real time to answer instead of a flat eight seconds, a dead link is walked past to the next source rather than ending playback, and when nothing can play it tells you which sources never answered instead of claiming nobody has the episode
- **Dub played sub.** Switching to dub handed back whichever stream came first, and Aniyomi sources showed only one cut because the sub/dub marker sits in the video's own title
- **Manga pages kept being thrown away.** A page you had just read had to be downloaded and decoded again the moment you scrolled back. Pages now fade in, and the loading placeholder no longer flashes grey blocks
- **The home banner overflowed smaller screens.** It was a fixed height that happened to suit a tall phone — on a shorter one it swallowed the screen and the dock sat on top of the page dots. The header could also land on the artwork on phones with a tall notch
- **"Mark this and all above as watched" sat off the bottom of the screen**, with no way to scroll to it
- **The app froze after tapping Solve Cloudflare**, if you had a lot of sources installed

### Improved

- **Searching and resolving no longer fight with the screen** on Android, so browsing stays smooth while sources are working
- **Seasons in the Relations tab.** A franchise split across several entries lists them in order, with real season numbers where they're known. Each season stays its own title, with its own progress and tracking

### Android TV

- **A dead stream moves to the next source on its own**, up to three, instead of stopping to ask
- The longer time limit for a source you picked, and the clearer failure messages, apply here too

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.1.0
cuerpo.body:
Episode lists that actually say what the episode is, a TV that behaves like one, and a long list of things that quietly didn't work.

### New

- **Episode lists carry real information.** Titles, ratings, runtimes, air dates and synopses stay put instead of being flattened into "Episode 1, Episode 2, Episode 3" the moment a source loads. The source only decides what can play — the catalogue decides what it's called
- **Crash reports come to us.** A crash takes the app with it, so the in-app log never gets to say what happened. Crashes now report themselves, which is how the resume bug in this release was found
- **Send a diagnostic log in one tap.** Settings › Advanced › Share logs uploads it and hands you a short code, instead of dropping a file into a share sheet and hoping. Secrets are stripped before anything leaves the phone
- **The reader hides the system bars**, so a page is the whole screen

### Improved

- **Android TV settings are one flow now**, with back transitions that go where you expect and sections that match the phone
- **Simkl tracking works.** It never sent the season, so a multi-season series sat on whatever episode it last recorded — S3E3 and S1E3 both read as "3". It also counts distinct episodes rather than a high-water mark, so a single scrobble left an account twelve episodes in reading "Watching · 1". Both fixed, and every scrobble is now logged either way
- **A source that times out gets another chance.** Pressing play on an episode clears the "too slow" mark instead of leaving that source benched for ten minutes
- **Cast and Relations load on their own** rather than waiting behind the episode list
- **Manga and novels stop sweeping every source** they were never going to match
- Active Source left Settings. It was a second copy of what the Sources screen already does
- The log file stopped rewriting itself on every single line — 326ms down to 69ms per 500 lines

### Fixed

- **Dub never played.** The toggle was built from counts the catalogue doesn't carry, so it had nothing to offer, the category never reached the source, and sub and dub shared one cache entry. Downloads had the same shape and ignored the source you picked
- **Switching source kept playing the old one**
- **A TV series could lose every episode it could actually play**, when the source's rows and the catalogue's rows disagreed about seasons
- **Leaving a video mid-load left the app hunting in the background**, so it felt frozen
- **Leaving a video could crash it** a few seconds later — a resume timer woke up and seeked a player that was already gone
- **Hold-to-speed threw away the speed you'd picked.** Set 2x, hold to skip, let go, and you were back at 1x
- **A chapter that failed to load showed a black screen** and said there were no pages. It retries now, and says what actually happened
- **The page count lied about how long a chapter was**
- **One flaky segment killed a whole download** and threw away everything already fetched. Segments retry, and a 404 still fails fast
- **Continue Watching was one list per mode**, so switching modes hid what you were watching
- The Cloudflare solver opened before anything had asked for it
- Simkl stopped burning through its daily request limit
- Provider logs went missing from shared reports, and installs and restores left no trace at all

### Android TV

- Settings pages have proper back transitions
- D-pad reaches the repo list instead of jumping straight to Add repo
- The providers search box stops opening the keyboard just because it got focus
- Seek pills take focus and respond to OK
- The Sub/Dub menu selects the cut you picked, and the checkmark follows
- "Wrong title?" stops closing when you release OK
- An overflow that clipped the layout

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v2.0.0
cuerpo.body:
Browse by what a show *is*, not by which source has it. Plus the first iOS and Apple TV builds.

### New

- **Browse from the catalogue, not the source.** Home, search and detail come from a metadata provider, and a source is matched underneath only when you press play. Titles, art, cast and relations stay right whatever you have installed
- **Pick your catalogue** — AniList or MyAnimeList for anime, manga and novels; TMDB or Simkl for movies and TV. If the one you picked is unreachable the other answers, and the app tells you it did. Switch it straight from the logo on Home
- **Auto Resolve.** You don't pick a source any more — the app sweeps your installed ones in your order and plays the first that has it. A show then remembers what played it. Pin one by hand whenever you'd rather choose
- **Source Priority, reworked** — order the sweep yourself, switch off the ones you never want tried, and see which of your sources actually has an episode before you press anything
- **Genres** — a new card on Home opens a grid of every genre, and tapping one drops you into search already filtered. On TV it's in Search, and a genre opens a paginated grid
- **Arrange your own Home.** A rows editor in Settings, per provider layout, with live save and reset. Tracker rows are merged in, so your AniList/MAL/Simkl lists sit alongside everything else
- **The app speaks 8 languages**, with a picker on phone and TV
- **Pick the app's font** — a few ship with the app, the rest download on demand
- **Use your own subtitle font**, alongside the built-in styling
- **Score on catalogue posters**, from whichever provider you're using
- **A source's own settings, drawn inside the app** — no more being thrown into a separate screen that looks like a different app
- **Trackers get their own screens**, and My List is yours again. Custom lists belong to the mode you made them in
- **Pinned sources** on the Sources tab
- **Sign in to a source from the list** — open its site, stay signed in, and clear just that site's cookies
- **See all** on the tracker rows and New Episodes, with paging as you scroll
- **Catalogue filters** — genre, year, season, format, status, score, plus an 18+ toggle that now follows your Privacy setting instead of resetting every search
- **Choose which title language AniList shows** (romaji, English or native)
- **Swipe between library tabs**, and pick which screen the app opens on
- Audio tracks are named by language and channel count, not "Track 2"
- The dock gives way while you scroll, so a long page isn't reading around it
- Android TV: **settings grouped into labelled sections**, episode progress scrobbles from the native TV players, and Home, search and browse now match the phone

### Improved

- The metadata search screen was rebuilt around recent searches and a filtered browse
- **"Wrong title?" is a grid of posters now.** When a source answers with five results all called the same thing, the cover is the only thing that tells them apart — so it's the whole row
- **Where to watch** names the provider and repo behind each result, and times them
- Errors say what actually went wrong, including offline and rate limits, instead of a blank screen
- Genres now come from AniList itself rather than a hand-written list, so it can't go stale
- Movies and TV rows carry their genres, which they never used to
- Schedule dropped the month view — the calendar only ever had about two weeks of real data, so the rest was blank by design. Movies & TV scrolls properly now on a day with hundreds of releases
- A source that has nothing for a title offers you a way out instead of a dead end

### Fixed

- **Downloads didn't work at all** on catalogue titles. Every one failed on "Resolve failed"
- **Nothing downloaded from some sources** because a playlist file was being saved as if it were the episode. Those are skipped now, and the app moves to a source that has a real file
- **Anime sources were searched first for films and live-action series** — and your saved Source Priority was quietly overriding the ordering entirely
- **CloudStream sources only showed their first six rows.** Every row shows now
- **"Wrong title?" re-pointed every other show**, not just the one you were fixing
- **AniList calls were all failing** and quietly falling back to the other provider. Titles, rows and search are AniList's data again
- **Episodes were picked by counting**, so one recap or special in the list shifted every episode after it. They're matched by number now
- One slow source could freeze the sweep; it's bounded now
- Cloudflare challenges are surfaced on detail, and solved against the domain the plugin actually uses
- The Cloudflare solver was handing people the raw site, and a plain block was being answered with a solver
- The player forgot which audio track you chose and only remembered its language
- The notification panel wouldn't open while watching, and the old screen bled into a rotation
- A source that never started now gets moved on from
- Scrambled manga sources drew their pages torn into squares, and "next chapter" left your scanlation group
- Subtitle outline styling never reached the renderer
- The DNS setting didn't survive a restart, and MAL's Trending and Popular this season were the same query
- Backup keeps your Source Priority order
- Metadata titles opened the wrong way from Play mirror, sharing, and TV pagination
- A tracker entry with no MAL id opened search instead of the title
- Custom lists appeared in every mode instead of the one they were made in
- Simkl series scrobbled as films, and Simkl series wouldn't open
- Manga chapters downloaded from a source that didn't have them, and manga detail lost most of its metadata
- Android TV: **App language and Search layout had become unreachable**, a Next button did nothing, dialogs had no visible focus, Back couldn't be reached by D-pad or would re-open detail, and a source's settings couldn't be opened with the remote

---

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.9.8
cuerpo.body:
A rebuilt reader, offline manga and novels, and a bottom bar you arrange yourself.

### New
- **Offline manga and novels** — download chapters the same way you download episodes, and read them with no connection
- The reader is rebuilt: **auto-scroll** in both readers, a floating pill for the controls, a chapter picker, volume keys to turn the page, and pull past the end to change chapter
- **Tap zones you choose** — decide what tapping each part of the page does, per reader
- Novel typography: letter and word spacing, background dimming, and an end-of-chapter page in the paged modes
- Webtoons switch to continuous mode on their own
- **New-chapter alerts** for manga and novel sources, alongside the episode ones
- **Choose which tabs the bottom bar shows** — reorder them, hide what you don't use, add Downloads or History
- **Cast and relations for manga and novels** — tap a creator to see everything else they've worked on
- **Open a video file from any other app** — Zangetsu now shows up in Android's "Open with" list
- **Material You** — the app takes its colours from your wallpaper
- **Custom categories in My List**, synced to your account, plus AniList custom lists and sorting on every list
- Search tells you **why** a source came back empty instead of spinning forever
- Sub/Dub badge and the source's claimed quality on posters while you browse
- Manga rows name the **scanlation group**, and the chapter list can filter by it
- **Skip the "previously on" recap**, alongside the existing OP and ED skips
- Open, copy or remove each tracker entry straight from the tracking sheet, and see at a glance when a title is already tracked
- A **Max (300s)** video buffer for flaky connections
- Classic is the default launcher icon again
- Android TV: **50-episode range chips** on detail and in the player, an **aspect-ratio switch**, caption styling, settings drill-ins and a speed pill

### Improved
- **Settings search finds the actual setting.** Searching "autoplay" used to hand you the Playback folder; now it finds *Autoplay next episode*. Things like "anime4k" found nothing at all before
- **Source health is honest** — a source is judged on several titles instead of one, so a slow or picky source isn't written off as dead
- A stream that was taking 38 seconds to start now starts promptly — it was probing audio tracks nobody asked for
- Picking an external player lists **every** video app you have installed, not a hardcoded few
- Aniyomi sources get their request timeouts back, so a stalled source gives up instead of hanging
- List entrances are visible now, with three styles to pick from, and the My List grid animates
- Android TV: D-pad focus is obvious across lists, chips, posters, settings and the source screens

### Fixed
- Cloudflare-gated **novel sources load** again, and novel plugins can read response headers
- Simkl's **"Wrong title?"** actually returns results — it had never worked, for any kind
- **Backup includes the settings it was quietly leaving out** — reader, theme, navigation, search layout and more
- MANGA Plus no longer kills the app on search
- CloudStream plugin dialogs never appeared; they do now
- The player's quality menu was switching **servers** instead of quality
- Subtitle translation works again after Google blocked the client we were sending
- Quality shows for DASH streams, not just HLS
- Schedule's My List filter matches by title when a show has no MAL id
- Downloads record their size and tidy up after themselves when they finish
- Android TV: the buffer setting reaches the TV players, Add Repo dialogs open the keyboard, ad segments no longer confuse the HLS probe, tracker libraries show on My List, and long-hold works on Home posters
- CloudStream sources are no longer told they're running on a TV when they aren't

### Also in this build
Apple TV (tvOS) support has landed in the codebase and is **still in beta** — not yet
part of a public tvOS release. Some of that work touched shared TV layout code, so
Android TV users are getting new viewport scaling in this build.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.9.7
cuerpo.body:
Discord Rich Presence, a rebuilt player bar, and tracking you can actually steer.

### New
- Discord Rich Presence — your profile shows **Watching**, the episode name, a poster and a live progress bar, and clears when you leave the player. Opt in from Settings → Discord
- Tracking now lists your trackers one by one, showing what each matched and how far along it thinks you are — edit them separately, or use **Sync all at once** as before
- **Auto-track** switch — stop AniList/MAL/Simkl being written to as you watch, without disconnecting them. On by default, so nothing changes unless you turn it off
- Long-press an episode to pick a player, reload its links, mark it watched, mark everything above it, or start on a specific mirror
- The detail screen tells you when the next episode airs
- Real episode names, where AniZip or TMDB has them — `Episode 18 · Break in! Button Hook Entry`
- Portrait toggle in the player, and the whole bottom bar can be reordered or have buttons hidden
- Proper controls inside the picture-in-picture window
- Right-to-left text in the novel reader
- iOS builds for TestFlight

### Improved
- The player bar is one compact row — episode skip in the centre, discs behind the transport buttons, tooltips on the icon-only controls, and a switch for swipe-to-seek
- Filler episodes are badged on Android TV too, and auto-skip now applies to the Next button as well as autoplay
- Touch-screen TVs: tap to show the controls, drag the seek bar, and one tap fires a button instead of two
- Discord Rich Presence reports from the Android TV players too, not just the phone
- Manga pages warm to disk instead of being decoded up front, so opening a chapter is quicker and uses less memory
- Manga and novels say **Reading**, not Watching
- Settings, sources, detail and the TV home screen split into smaller files — no behaviour change, just easier to work on

### Fixed
- A wrong tracker match is visible and fixable at last — the sheet names what it matched, and the fix-it link now appears for manga and novels, where it was missing entirely
- Two trackers holding different episode counts no longer flatten each other silently; you get told, and the higher number wins
- External players work with Cloudflare-protected streams
- Downloaded episodes play through the TV player instead of falling back to mpv
- Mirrors that were seconds from arriving are no longer cancelled
- Android TV: episodes that fail to load say so, a held OK opens My List options, recent searches can be cleared, and the remote can leave the sign-in fields
- Android TV starts the video without waiting on episode names first — on a cold cache over slow wifi that meant staring at a black screen
- The player fills the screen on phones with a display cutout
- Picture-in-picture showed the wrong play/pause icon
- Short novel chapters no longer crash the text-direction check
- A shared link carries its cover image
- The pairing QR uses https, so an iPhone camera can open it

---

Thanks to [@NeighborhoodNerd](https://github.com/NeighborhoodNerd) for the Discord Rich Presence work, iOS support, and a run of Android TV fixes in this release.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.9.4 — Manga, Novels & a Refreshed Home
cuerpo.body:
## Zangetsu v1.9.4 — Manga, Novels & a Refreshed Home

**📖 Manga mode.** Zangetsu now reads manga. Install Mihon extensions from the sources screen, then browse, search and read manga right in the app — with its own source picker, per-title tracking, and reading history. Continue Reading picks up the chapter you left off on.

The video mode is now labelled **Streaming**, since it covers anime, movies and series.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.9.3 — Black-Screen Fix, Episode Details & Working Source Filters
cuerpo.body:
## Zangetsu v1.9.3 — Black-Screen Fix, Episode Details & Working Source Filters

**📺 A fix for the black video some phones have had since 1.9.0.** If playback ran with sound and controls but no picture, and changing source or decoder made no difference, this is for you. mpv's GPU renderer can't run on some older GPUs, and nothing in the app let you avoid it. **Settings → Playback → Video renderer** now does: pick **MediaCodec Embed** and the phone's decoder draws straight to the screen, skipping the renderer entirely. Defaults to Auto, so nothing changes unless you need it. (On that renderer Anime4K and subtitle styling are unavailable.)

**⏭️ Auto-skip openings and endings.** Two new toggles in **Settings → Playback**. Off by default. Each opening skips once per episode, so seeking back to actually watch it doesn't bounce you out again.

**🔎 Aniyomi source filters now work.** Setting a source's Sort / Genre / Year filters with an empty search box used to do nothing at all — the selection was saved and ignored. It now browses the source with those filters, keeps loading more as you scroll, and the filter sheet no longer collapses when the keyboard appears.

**📝 Richer episode lists.** Real episode titles, stills, runtime and ratings pulled from AniZip/TMDB, plus a description on each episode row. Cached to disk and prefetched when you tap, so the detail screen fills in faster.

**🔍 Better search.** Results are ranked by how well they match what you typed, source rows are ordered best-first, and repeat searches return faster.

**📚 Library & trackers.**
- Per-title tracker edit sheet from My List.
- Optionally add a title to My List automatically when you start playing it.
- Simkl now shows movies and TV in your library, not just anime, and matches on every available id.
- Anime that movie sources mislabel now scrobbles correctly.

**⚙️ Settings redesign.** Grouped, drill-down sections instead of one long page, with a compact header on the deeper screens. History gets its own row. You can edit your display name, and extensions can auto-update.

**⏰ Sleep timer.** Added a 5-minute option, an on-screen indicator, and it can close the app entirely.

**🐛 Fixes.**
- **My List no longer breaks completely** because of one item it can't read — the rest of your list loads, and cloud sync no longer stops halfway.
- A minimal number-wheel download sheet as an alternative to the grid.
- Close-confirmation modes for the player: double-back, confirm, or exit straight away.

---

*This is a pre-release. Turn on **Beta updates** in Settings to get builds like this early.*

### Which APK do I download?
- **Phone:** `arm64-v8a` (most phones) or `armeabi-v7a` (older 32-bit phones). Not sure? Use `universal`.
- **Android TV / Fire TV:** `tv` (works on any TV, 32-bit or 64-bit).
- **universal** works on everything but is larger.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.7.0 — Schedule, Aniyomi & a New TV Player
cuerpo.body:
## ✨ What's new

**📅 Schedule tab**
A brand-new Schedule tab — a compact **weekly anime airing calendar** (what's on today and all week, with live countdowns) plus **upcoming movies & TV**. Tap anything to find it across your sources. Available on phone and Android TV.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.6.0 — Android TV, Torrents & Backup
cuerpo.body:
### 🎉 New

- 📺 **Android TV support** — the whole app now works on TV with a remote: D-pad navigation everywhere, on-screen keyboard search, and a full TV player.
- 🧲 **Torrent support** — play and download magnet / `.torrent` sources. Streams start while downloading; offline downloads keep going in the background and save into your folder. (Wi-Fi-only by default — toggle in Settings › Torrents.)
- 💾 **Backup & Restore** — save your sources, library & settings to a file and restore them any time (Settings › Backup & Restore).
- 📂 **Choose your download folder** — pick any folder for downloads (SD card supported), plus a new Downloads tab with collapsible groups, search, and a storage summary.

### ✨ Improvements

- **Sharing** — share any title with a deep link that opens straight to it in the app.
- **Forgot password** — reset via email with a branded reset page.
- **Settings redesign** — cleaner, organized into clear sections.
- **In-app diagnostic log** — Settings › Share logs, to send a log if you hit an issue.

### ⚡ Performance & reliability

- **Much lighter on data & cloud usage** — smaller, cached avatars, throttled library sync, and far fewer background writes, so sync stays reliable.
- **My List self-heals** — items added while offline sync up automatically once you're back online.
- **CloudStream fixes** — more sources install and show their own settings; torrent sources no longer dropped; clearer install errors.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.5.0 — Watch Party, Auto Subtitles & Source Updates
cuerpo.body:
## ✨ What's new in 1.5.0

### 👥 Watch Party
Watch together with friends in perfect sync. Create or join a room and everyone follows the host's play / pause / seek live. Includes in‑player text chat, a participants list, request‑to‑control, and automatic host hand‑off if the host drops.

### 💬 Auto subtitles
Subtitles now **auto‑select your preferred language** and download a matching track automatically — including Indian languages (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Urdu, Malayalam) alongside the usual English/European ones. Pick your language in **Settings → Playback**.

### 🔄 CloudStream source updates
Installed CloudStream sources now tell you when an update is available — with a per‑source **Update** button, **Update all**, and an optional **"source updates available"** notification on launch. Toggle it in **Settings → Notifications**.

### ➕ More sources, faster
- One‑tap **recommended CloudStream repos** in the "CS Add repo" dialog.
- Same‑named extensions from **different repos** can now be installed side by side.
- Recently‑resolved stream links are cached briefly, so re‑opening an episode starts almost instantly.

### ▶️ Player
- Added **SPlayer** to the external‑player options.
- **Resume** is far more reliable — it actually picks up where you left off, even on flaky hosts.

### 🛠️ Fixes & polish
- In‑app updates download the **right APK for your device** and verify it — fixes "package appears to be invalid".
- Downloads **retry & resume** instead of restarting from 0 on flaky hosts.
- CloudStream plugin settings, Stremio add‑ons, and source labels (origin repo) fixed up.
- Cloudflare clearances persist across restarts.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.4.0 — Smarter Search, Source Health & Title Logos

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.2.0
cuerpo.body:
Zangetsu v1.2.0

  Changes since v1.1.0.

  Player

  - Volume slider reworked: 0–100% sets the system volume, above 100% adds a software boost (up to 200%,
  shown in red).
  - Pinch to zoom (up to 4×) with pan; double-tap to seek now shows a ripple at the tap point.
  - Brightness/volume indicator moved to a vertical bar on the side you swipe.
  - Shows the poster while a stream loads instead of a black screen.
  - "Up next" card now shows the next episode's thumbnail, plus a Next Episode button near the end.
  - Auto-switches to another server if a stream stalls mid-playback, resuming at the same time.
  - Subtitle styling (font, colour, background, position, size) with 10 bundled fonts, plus online
  subtitle search.
  - Remembers playback speed and quality per title.
  - Hardware decoding enabled; faster playback start.
  - Audio normalisation option.

  Sources

  - Support for Cloudflare-protected sources (e.g. AnimePahe).
  - Per-source settings (domain picker, etc.).
  - Sub/Dub selection for CS anime.
  - HLS playback fixes for disguised / multi-host CDNs.

  Downloads

  - Fixed downloads restarting from 0% on unstable hosts — they now retry and resume from where they left
  off.

  App

  - In-app updates: checks GitHub for new versions and installs them from here on.
  - Detail screen transitions and small UI fixes.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.1.0 --- CloudStream support , so many changes
cuerpo.body:
Zangetsu v1.1.0

  The biggest update yet — CloudStream extension support lands, plus Picture-in-Picture, full tracker
  sync, Cast & Relations, and a pile of player and download improvements.

    CloudStream support (new!)
  - Add a repo, then install the sources you want — one by one (no auto-installing the whole repo).
  - CloudStream sources work in Home, Search, Details, and playback (with subtitles).
  - Enable/disable individual sources, check for updates, remove a repo — from a clean, grouped
  CloudStream tab.
  - Tracker sync + Cast/Relations for CloudStream titles too (AniList/MAL for anime, Simkl for
  movies/series); when a source has no IDs, Zangetsu resolves it via TMDB so it still tracks and shows
  full cast + related titles.
  - Faster home loading and a clear "couldn't load" message for dead sources.

   Search — CloudStream sources now appear in results, plus a per-source search picker (categorised
  Anime / Movies & Series / NSFW) to switch sources off for search only.

   Player — Picture-in-Picture (Android) with a PiP button + auto-PiP setting, and external player
  support with automatic fallback to the built-in player.

   Trackers — AniList, MyAnimeList & Simkl auto-scrobble for anime, movies and series.

   Details — new Cast and Relations tabs with photos and tap-to-open related titles.

   Downloads — offline soft subtitles and a Sub/Dub selector.

   Other — redesigned source switcher, cleaner Settings, "See All" grids, NSFW gate, provider
  cache-busting, and assorted fixes.

cuerpo.name: Zangetsu v1.0.0 — first release.
cuerpo.body:
## Highlights
- Anime and movie/series streaming with an in-app source switcher
- Player: gesture controls (brightness/volume), scrub preview, skip intro, sub/dub, quality selection, subtitles
- My List and Continue Watching with cross-device sync
- Offline downloads
- Sources included out of the box: AllAnime and HiAnime (anime); 4K HDHub, UHD Movies, and HDHub4u (movies and series)
